label: hood bypass gap
description:
An opening around a still-installed filter that lets air bypass the filter media, confirmed by seeing the dark plenum or rack space BEHIND the filter plane through the opening. If a whole panel is gone, that is a missing filter, not a bypass gap.
Look hardest at: the two END panels where they meet the hood's side frame or wall; and any filter that is tilted, bowed, recessed, protruding, dislodged, off its track, bent, or has a cracked/damaged baffle channel—these create an opening that exposes the space behind the filter plane.
The decisive test is depth: through the opening you must be able to see actual space, plenum, or rack behind the filter plane. The opening may be small, but that depth must be visible.
Do NOT apply for: the normal vertical baffle channels inside a single intact filter; a thin flush seam or plain line between two properly seated adjacent panels where no depth behind is visible; reflections, highlights, dark bands, or colored shapes on the filter face; handles, frame rails, or grease staining by themselves; or an entirely empty slot (missing filter).
In the classification explanation, identify which filter/edge the opening is at and the visible depth behind the filter plane that distinguishes it from a plain seam or a reflection.
